day_shape: CENTCOM confirms 12pm ET strikes on IRGC targets in Iran with Bandar Abbas, Chabahar and Konarak reporting explosions, Brent above $94, IDF/Shin Bet capture Hamas internal security chief Muein al-Arabid in Gaza City, and FinCEN proposes 311 measure against Banque Misr UAE.

threads.label: US strikes on southern Iran
threads.summary: CENTCOM announced US forces began striking IRGC targets in Iran at 12pm ET, citing recent IRGC attempts against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and US personnel, with Jerusalem Post reporting strikes on Bandar Abbas. Iranian state channels reported explosions in Chabahar, Konarak, Qeshm, Sirik and Bandar Abbas, and Trump posted on Truth Social warning Iran against retaliation.

threads.label: Iranian retaliation threats and posture
threads.summary: Iran's General Staff and Khatam al-Anbiya headquarters vowed "crushing and devastating blows" in response to US strikes on Sistan and Baluchestan and Hormozgan, and the IRGC spokesman said "a harsh punishment awaits the aggressors," per Defa Press and IRIB. Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf claimed 15 months of military progress equivalent to a decade, and Jerusalem Post cited Iran International reporting IRGC Unit 4000 planning operations against the Straits of Malacca and Bangka.

threads.label: Pezeshkian diplomacy at SCO summit
threads.summary: Iran International and Jerusalem Post reported President Pezeshkian said Iran would immediately reciprocate if Washington returned to the June Islamabad interim deal, while Speaker Ghalibaf vowed to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed. Foreign Minister Araghchi, quoted by Defa Press and IRIB from the Bishkek SCO summit, said Iran will not act before the US does, and Pezeshkian thanked Putin for solidarity.

threads.label: Capture of Hamas internal security chief
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet announced special forces raided a building in Gaza City and captured Muein al-Arabid, described as the head of Hamas's internal security apparatus, with Netanyahu confirming the operation. Arabic-language and Palestinian media claimed an Israeli-backed anti-Hamas militia carried out the raid with Israeli air support, according to Times of Israel and Jerusalem Post.

threads.label: Gaza strikes and Lebanon activity
threads.summary: The IDF said it struck a Hamas military-wing commander in Jabalia, citing systematic ceasefire violations, and reported locating anti-tank missiles, launchers and explosives in the southern Lebanon Security Zone. Jerusalem Post reported Kaja Kallas said more than 10 EU member states are willing to contribute to a new mission to train Lebanese forces.

threads.label: Hormuz shipping and oil market
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported two supertankers carrying Saudi oil were struck by unknown projectiles minutes apart while transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz, and CENTCOM said US forces have redirected 84 commercial vessels, disabled 3 and boarded 2 enforcing the blockade on Iran. IRIB reported Brent crude rose more than 4% above $94 a barrel.

threads.label: Iran economy, sanctions and unrest
threads.summary: FinCEN issued a proposed rule under section 311 designating five UAE branches of Banque Misr as of primary money-laundering concern, while Iran's Central Bank Governor Hemmati said Iran has sufficient reserves and is ready to inject $2 billion to stabilise the rial. Jerusalem Post reported security forces beat and fired on jobseekers protesting in Gachsaran, per human rights groups.

events.title: Proposal of Special Measure Regarding Banque Misr UAE as a Financial Institution Operating Outside of the United States of Primary Money Laundering Concern
events.summary: FinCEN is issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking, pursuant to section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act, that finds the five United Arab Emirates-based branches of Banque Misr (collectively, Banque Misr UAE) to be of primary money laundering concern and proposes imposing a special measure to: prohibit U.S. financial institutions from opening or maintaining a correspondent account for, or on behalf of, Banque Misr UAE; require U.S. financial institutions to take reasonable steps not to process a transaction for the correspondent account in the United States of a foreign banking institution if such a transaction involves Banque Misr UAE; and require U.S. financial institutions to apply special due diligence to their foreign correspondent accounts that are reasonably designed to guard against their use to process transactions involving Banque Misr UAE.
